criteria.label: Liberal/conservative political preference
criteria.definition: Own tendency to vote for liberal versus conservative candidates in the declared source cultural context; not generic change preference.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays leaning/voting for liberal political candidates or a clearly liberal political orientation.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays leaning/voting for conservative candidates or a clearly conservative political orientation.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Political labels can vary across countries/time; report declared meaning. Reform or continuity alone is weaker indirect evidence, not an automatic substitute. A label-linked own preference is content even without policy expertise; no real candidate endorsement advice.

criteria.label: Absolute moral standards
criteria.definition: Belief about existence of absolute right/wrong, preserving frozenOR/currentAND variant; not merely acknowledging context-sensitive application.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays rejecting an absolute moral right/wrong foundation or believing moral rightness has no context-independent absolute standard.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays a stable absolute right/wrong foundation even while applications require context.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Moral uncertainty or tolerant disagreement alone is null. A contextual application can coexist with absolute principles; keep mixed cases rather than assuming all nuance is high.

criteria.label: Help, punishment and toughness on crime
criteria.definition: Preference for helping criminals versus punishment, views on excessive coddling and being tough on crime; consequential/general cases retained.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays help/rehabilitation preferred over punishment and rejects excessive punitive emphasis.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays criminals being coddled too much, favoring tougher crime response or punishment over help.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Victim concern, safety or efficacy can coexist; not automatic confounded-only exclusions of explicit general stance. One punishment passage gets one dimension grade, not additional enforcement grade unless distinct rule-enforcement evidence.

criteria.label: One true religion
criteria.definition: Belief that one religion is uniquely true versus rejecting that exclusivity; allows multiple or no religion being true.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays rejecting a uniquely true religion, including pluralism or belief that none is uniquely true.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays belief in one true religion, even if respectful to other believers.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Civility, interfaith participation, lack of knowledge or uncertainty alone are null. Atheism can be opposite content if explicit exclusivity is rejected, not automatically converted to pluralist spirituality.

criteria.label: Tax support for artists
criteria.definition: Judgment that too much tax money supports artists versus rejecting that claim; spending attitudes not only artistic taste.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays tax support for artists as worthwhile/not excessive.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays tax support for artists as too much/excessive or unjustified public spending.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Art enjoyment, budget description or abstract feasibility alone is null; fiscal/value reasons may coexist and do not invalidate literal spending judgment. No policy fact/real budget assumed.

criteria.label: Strict law enforcement
criteria.definition: Belief that laws should be strictly enforced versus favoring discretion/less strict enforcement; not restricted to harmless technical violations.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays support for contextual discretion or rejecting uniformly strict enforcement.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays belief in strict enforcement of laws, including consequential cases.
criteria.mixed_or_null: A particular crime punishment belongsR3 unless distinct law-enforcement standard stated. Conscience/rule compliance C3 differs from a general enforcement-policy belief. Safety reasons may explain a stance without erasing it.

criteria.label: Standing for national anthem
criteria.definition: Liking to stand during a national anthem and attachment to that actual gesture; not only generic civic ceremony.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays little liking/attachment to standing for the anthem, preferring another choice or rejecting personal participation.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays liking/wanting to stand for the anthem, with its national/traditional meaning.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Physical incapacity alone is null. Generic ceremonial tolerance or other patriotic ritual is indirect; explicit anthem-standing preference counts. Political dissent/religious reasons can coexist and are recorded, not blanket invalidation.

boundary_controls.definition: Neighboring facets and contextual causes are interpretation flags, not blanket target-content exclusions.
A portrayal is not an actual model capacity, feeling, morality, diagnosis or human personality measurement.
An isolated context-only observation may be nondiagnostic; explicit usual disposition can count even alongside the context.

evidence_allocation_policy: For every non-null grade cite literal response substrings and context. Allocate a shared passage to the best-fitting primary substantive dimension; other overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or piece of evidence supports them. Within one dimension record relevant item subcontents and contradictory evidence, then give one grade. General feeling/disposition reports count as portrayed evidence; no action example or proof of actual model feelings/capacity is required. Distinct clauses may evidence multiple dimensions. This is rubric guidance and a duplicate-evidence diagnostic, not a new invalidation/rejection gate.
scoring_formula: Grades−2..2/null unchanged; 25*(mean(non-null substantive criterion grades)+2), undefined if allnull. Numeric75/25/gap50 unchanged. Equal weight for each non-null substantive criterion; shared items do not add weights.

grades.null: absent or non-discriminating evidence; not grade0

quality_interpretation: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.

eligibility.implementation: Frozen V3 scorer; four automatic quality exclusions. Hostility is descriptive only. Numeric and evidence rules retained.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; no second experimental rater or retrospective rejudge. Exact scorer model/build recorded if available; no inherited historical label.
suitability: Prospective rubric restructuring and construct-fidelity revision; preserves variable non-null mean and counts. This does not establish validity or equal psychological scales.

approved_eligibility_amendment.change: Hostility removed from automatic eligibility exclusion
